steps.name: Lay in the forest floor

lines.text: Let the far woods and the misty sky dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is at the bottom edge, and its left side is about 3/4 in from the left edge; it's about 12 in wide and 5 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the autumn leaves, and the birches' shading and bark patches will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the misty sky and the fir trees, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paints, darkest first: Leaf brown, then Golden ochre. The paint map shows where each goes.
Mix enough Leaf brown for this step and step 9; cover it between them.
Keep the brush level and the strokes long, left and right.
It should leave flat, level bands that seem to stretch away, with slight streaks that follow the stroke.

steps.meant: The lower third of the canvas is a flat ground, golden ochre at the back darkening to leaf brown in front, with no path, leaves or rock.

steps.name: Pull the path back into the mist

lines.text: Let the forest floor and the far woods dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 2 in from the bottom edge, and its right side is about 5 1/2 in from the right edge; it's about 2 in wide and 1 1/2 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the autumn leaves and the sunlit leaves on the ground will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the forest floor and the misty sky, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Mark one dot on the horizon. Draw three to five faint chalk or pencil lines fanning out from it. Pull each row's strokes along its line, wide in front and thin near the dot.
It should leave bands that narrow and bunch together toward one point, which is what makes the ground lie down and recede.
Watch out: Rows run parallel or cross each other. Fix: mark the dot and the fan of lines first. It takes a minute.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: A mauve-brown path runs from the bottom center back into the mist, wide in front and a thin thread at the back. No leaves on it yet.
